authority: Severity reflects what a failure actually costs. HARD_FAIL blocks the release. STRONG_WARNING and SOFT_WARNING report and do not block. Unclassified checks default to STRONG_WARNING so an unreviewed check cannot silently gate a release.

severity_definitions.HARD_FAIL: Blocks the release. Money, secrets, legal exposure, or structural integrity of published pages.
severity_definitions.STRONG_WARNING: Reported prominently, does not block. Quality and hygiene.

validators.reason: authority contracts govern what may publish
broken checkout or product binding costs real revenue

validators.command: npm run validate:commerce && npm run validate:authority && npm run validate:downloads && npm run validate:secrets
validators.reason: composite: commerce, authority, downloads
conversion and admin surfaces must resolve
legal disclaimers are non-negotiable on published pages
paid customers must receive the file they bought
missing environment configuration breaks the deploy
stub content must never reach a live page
release evidence must match what shipped
validators.repair_rationale: validate:proof-readiness fails when artifacts/authority/admission-report.json and release-manifest.json no longer balance against data/authority/content_registry.json; authority:flow (scripts/authority/run-full-flow.mjs) is the script that regenerates both from that registry.

validators.reason: prevents publishing against synthetic queries with no demand evidence
validators.repair_rationale: validate:query-atlas fails with "missing data/authority_scale/query_atlas.json - run the atlas build first" when the generated atlas is absent or stale; atlas:build (scripts/atlas/build_query_atlas.mjs) is the script that writes that file from the evidence it validates.

validators.reason: leaked or missing credentials
canonical hosts and guide integrity affect every indexed page
validators.repair_command: npm run authority:flow && npm run search:diagnose && npm run search:repair
validators.repair_rationale: validate:seo reports "stale authority admission report" and "missing upward link registry", both regenerated by authority:flow, and "incomplete hub core: <slug>" when a hub in data/seo/hub_pages.json has no description - the exact field search:diagnose flags as hub_missing_meta_description and search:repair writes. Partial by design: the content-quality failures this validator also reports have no generated fix, and the loop re-validates and reports them by name.

validators.command: npm run validate:profile-purity && npm run validate:tree-hygiene && npm run validate:content && npm run validate:env && npm run validate:disclaimers && npm run validate:no-theater && npm run validate:no-stubs && npm run validate:contracts && npm run validate:conversion-admin && npm run validate:proof-readiness && npm run validate:seo && npm run validate:search-intelligence
validators.reason: composite: purity, hygiene, proof readiness, seo, authority
external-agent build directives rendered as page copy are visible defects and poison the text answer engines extract
an empty table cell breaks column-to-header alignment and makes the table unusable as a fact source
content quality signal; the SEO and authority gates block the real risks
measurement honesty check; reports rather than blocks
advisory copy-quality signal
profile drift should be corrected but does not break the site
observational signal, no live-site impact
working tree debris is a maintenance problem, not a release risk

repair_contract: A validator may declare repair_command only when that command fixes the same defect this validator detects. scripts/selfheal/heal_until_clean.mjs runs it on failure and re-validates. Pairing a repair with a validator it does not actually fix would turn the self-heal loop into a way of making failures disappear, so an unpaired validator is the correct and honest default.
